qt: to the Commission Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE) Subject:

The Baltic Sea region has experienced an increase in signal interference incidents in the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), including jamming and spoofing. Jamming blocks satellite navigation signals, while spoofing sends false signals that can provide incorrect positioning information. These disruptions create growing concerns for maritime safety, as ships rely on GNSS systems such as the Global Positioning System (GPS) and Galileo for navigation. The consequences of these incidents can include increased risks of maritime accidents, disruption to international trade and supply chains, as well as wider security concerns affecting critical infrastructure. 1.
Does the Commission consider the current EU maritime safety framework sufficient to address the increasing risks caused by GNSS interference in the Baltic Sea region?
What actions is the Commission taking to support the development of alternative or backup navigation systems to ensure safe maritime operations when GNSS signals are disrupted?
Does the Commission intend to increase investment in resilient navigation and communication technologies to strengthen EU maritime security?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) The EU maritime safety framework provides flexibility to respond to evolving challenges. Interference of positioning systems has significant impact on maritime, both ships and monitoring bodies. While interference has increased, so has the vigilance of seafarers and authorities. Safe navigation relies on a combination of tools, both digital and classic. Navigational officers are trained to adapt to the situation and select appropriate tools. Beyond the European Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), ships foremost use the Automatic Identification System (AIS), mandated by the International Maritime Organisation for convention ships. In 2024, the Commission1 established an ad-hoc maritime sub-group2 on AIS spoofing and interference, consisting of Member State experts, the Commission and supported by expertise in the European Maritime Safety Agency. Its scope is Europe-wide as interference may occur in any sea basin, while more reported in the Baltic and Black Sea. The first set of work concluded, delivering an incident reporting protocol through the Union Maritime Information and Exchange System to alert any mariners and aid navigational precautions. The group will continue and cooperate with the Commission Task Force on GNSS Radio Frequency Interference (RFI). Under the upcoming European Space Shield, the Commission will present an RFI action plan addressing jamming and spoofing, with concrete measures to strengthen the resilience of GNSS services. In the 2028–2034 European Competitiveness Fund, the Commission proposed EUR131 billion for security, defence and space would raise EU investment fivefold, creating significant opportunity to boost resilient navigation and communication technologies.
1 through the High-level Steering Group for governance of the digital maritime system and services, established
by Commission Decision (EU) 2016/566. 2 under the Vessel Traffic Monitoring and Information System Directive (2002/59/EC).
